identity.name: Big Pilot's Watch

case.bezel: no bezel — fixed black dial with oversized luminous numerals

identity.one_liner: A 46mm automatic with a 7-day power reserve, descended from 1940s observation watches built for military navigators rather than pilots' wrists.

provenance_events.description: IWC reissues the 1940s Beobachtungsuhr (B-Uhr) pilot's watch as the Big Pilot's Watch 5002 (later 5007, 5010) in 2002. The 46.2mm case, conical crown, and onion-style hands establish the modern "Big Pilot" aesthetic that runs to the present.

narrative.story: IWC's Big Pilot lineage traces to 1940s observation watches like the Caliber 52 T.S.C., a 55mm pocket-watch-sized instrument built for military navigators who needed a large, highly legible dial rather than a watch meant to be worn during flight. IWC reintroduced the concept as a wearable wristwatch in 2002, and the current Big Pilot's Watch keeps the oversized crown and dial legibility of the original while adding a 7-day power reserve indicator — a feature the 1940s version, read at a desk rather than worn, never needed to solve.
narrative.collector_notes: Confirm the exact movement generation (52010 vs. 52110 vs. later updates), since power-reserve indicator position and case-back engraving changed across updates without any change to the outward case design.
